identity: Editorial still-life in crimson, ochre and forest; bowls, a grove, an axe, a gate and a brake recur with specific meanings.
culturalBoundary: No antlered mascot or invented portrayal of living Indigenous teachings. Erysichthon axe is attributed to its Greek chapter. Hungry-ghost discussion uses an abstract loop rather than conflating religious figures.
sourceImages: Only cover art, inspected. Original tree motif evokes its living substrate without reproducing the cover.
causality: Appearances and spatial shifts follow the spoken distinctions; no quantitative chart invented.
themes: Pale materials in Dark, strong ink typography in every theme.
